_comment: M14.0.SPEC (#419) — html completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of the pinned wasm/tree-sitter-html.wasm (19 distinct; the grammar exposes 26 nodeTypeForId slots because start_tag/script_start_tag/style_start_tag and tag_name/erroneous_end_tag_name are ALIASED onto shared names) is in exactly one bucket. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type the wasm no longer produces is a stale row and also fails. NO OPEN GAPS: `raw_text` was the last one and the #288 wave closed it — 13 handled, 5 internal_silent, 1 design_decision = 19/19.

handled_verified.note: Fourteen types, each read in src/ast/real-html-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `document` supplies the module symbol's range and the walk root; `doctype` is recorded as `metadata.doctype` on that symbol. `quoted_attribute_value` and `attribute_value` are both read because the grammar nests the unquoted value INSIDE the quoted node, and an empty value has no inner node — the pure-String `unquote` fallback covers exactly that case. All three tag containers (`start_tag`, `self_closing_tag`, and the two aliased script/style forms that surface as `start_tag`) go through one `getStartTag` cursor. ERROR is the last RECOVERY type, and it was one of the two that section A left unclassified. It is read by name and it is LIVE: the html grammar does emit ERROR nodes, and the read has a three-part observable contract — the broken region is reported as a ParseError anchored to the ERROR NODE'S OWN span, the node is BYPASSED, and the elements around it still publish symbols, containment and their resource edges. All three halves are pinned by html/error-recovery, whose fixture places the error in the MIDDLE of the document so the half-after-the-error case is the one under test. Treating ERROR as silent would have been the convenient classification and would have been wrong: silence means 'correctly emits nothing', and this emits a diagnostic.

internal_silent.note: Five types that correctly emit nothing and need no analyzer read. `end_tag` needs none because the element's PUBLISHED range is the whole element node, whose span is defined by its start_tag..end_tag pair — reading the end_tag separately would produce the same line twice. `text` and `comment` are literals; `comment` is in the grammar's `extras`, so it appears between elements and is deliberately not a node. `erroneous_end_tag`/`erroneous_end_tag_name` are the grammar's mis-nesting RECOVERY shape: the analyzer reports the ERROR and does not model the recovered structure, because a fabricated tree for a mis-nested document would be a guess dressed as a fact. MISSING joins them on measurement rather than on assumption. The analyzer reads it defensively — `n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing` is one condition, and the `isMissing` half costs one property read per node — but NO html input produces a MISSING node. Twelve deliberately malformed documents were tried (unterminated comment, unterminated attribute quote, unterminated doctype, unclosed script/style/textarea/select/template, attribute with no value at EOF, a stray end tag, and `<>>><<></` soup) and the tree-sitter-html grammar recovered from every one of them without inserting a single token: it is fully error-tolerant in the way HTML is, so there is nothing for MISSING to be. The read is KEPT, because a grammar change could make it live and a one-property guard is not worth removing on the strength of today's grammar. This is the same split `bash` already records — ERROR handled, MISSING silent — reached independently and by measurement on both lanes, which is the useful part: two grammars, one ruling.

decisions.question: Should the analyzer decode character references by reading `entity` child nodes, or by decoding the attribute's own text? RULED: decode the TEXT, in pure-String. An `entity` is a child of `quoted_attribute_value`'s value span, so reading it would make the decoded value a per-fragment assembly rather than one string per attribute — and the analyzer's whole contract for an attribute is one decoded string (the value of `href="?a=1&b=2"` is one module name, not three fragments). It also keeps the ordering that matters for security: the decode runs BEFORE scheme detection, so `javascript:` and `javascript:` are recognised as `javascript:` rather than smuggled past a filter — measured on the scheme-and-navigation fixture, where the pre-fix bare `startsWith("javascript:")` missed both. An unknown or malformed reference is copied through VERBATIM, because dropping half a URL invents a different resource; the `odd-ref`, `no-semi` and `prose-amp` pins carry that half of the contract.
